note: FNS 1130.3 lists bills and provider statements as the standard verification for dependent care expenses. The OLG (Dependent Care Expenses Deduction > Verification of Dependent Care Expenses) explicitly treats dependent care as an 'optional verification' where 'a telephonic or written self-declaration of the dependent care expense is an acceptable verification unless the information appears questionable.' Documentary evidence (provider letter, canceled checks, day care voucher, third-party documentation) is only requested when the expense appears questionable. This is a materially different verification standard: FNS requires documentary evidence (bills, provider statements) as the baseline, while the OLG defaults to self-declaration and only escalates to documentary evidence when information is questionable. This likely reflects a deliberate Massachusetts policy choice to reduce verification burden, but it is a clear departure from the FNS standard.

_layer3.note: 106 CMR 364.450(B) explicitly permits verification of deductible expenses 'only when questionable' rather than as a standard requirement. This directly contradicts FNS Handbook 310 Section 1130.3, which lists bills and provider statements as standard (mandatory baseline) verification for dependent care. The CMR also references 106 CMR 361.620 (Questionable Information) as the threshold for requiring verification. Massachusetts has adopted a 'verify-if-questionable' standard for dependent care expenses, while FNS requires documentary evidence upfront. The OLG correctly implements the state regulation but diverges from the federal standard. This is a deliberate state policy choice—Massachusetts is using a state option to reduce verification burden below the federal minimum.
